items.title: Sleep
items.text: Regular bedtime and wake-up. Naps count toward the day
items.sub:
10 to 13 h (health office, nutrition society, WHO)
11 to 12 h (ministry guidelines)

items.title: Screens
items.text: Under 1 hour a day in all, less is better. None at bedtime
items.sub: Health commission, nutrition society and WHO agree

items.title: Outside
items.text: Run around outdoors every day. 2 hours here, and at weekends
items.sub: Outdoors comes first for the eyes

footnote: Source: Education ministry 2012, Patriotic Health office 2025, Nutrition Society 2022, WHO 2019, Health Commission 2021 (two papers), Work Regulations
notes: If you remember only three things tonight, make it these three, and stick them on the fridge. One, sleep enough: a regular bedtime and wake-up time, and naps count toward the day's sleep. Two, less screen time: the National Health Commission, the Chinese Nutrition Society and the World Health Organization all advise no more than an hour a day in total, and less is better. Three, get outside: children have two hours outdoors here every day, so keep it up at weekends and in the holidays. The exact hours differ a little between these bodies, and the next slide shows them side by side.
